cleanIntro: This guide follows FoldAR's own operator's manual, which covers the FoldAR family as a whole and prints no calibre or variant - check your rifle against that book. Below the folding barrel interface it strips like a standard AR-style rifle: two captive takedown pins, then the bolt carrier group out of the upper. FoldAR's book takes the owner as far as the bolt carrier group and the quick-detach barrel system, and no further.

steps.title: Magazine out - the button is on the right, above the trigger
steps.action: Point the rifle in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger. Press the magazine release button on the right side of the receiver above the trigger and remove the magazine, then pull the charging handle all the way back to remove any chambered cartridge.
steps.prose: Magazine before charging handle, every time, or the handle simply feeds the next round. Pull the handle the full length of its travel - a short pull can leave a round in the chamber. Do this with the rifle unfolded and the locking lever latched, the state FoldAR's own unloading procedure assumes.
steps.quote: First, press the magazine release button -on the right side of the firearm above the trigger- and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Unloading the Firearm, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)

steps.title: Lock the bolt carrier group to the rear
steps.action: With your left thumb pressing the bolt catch, pull the charging handle all the way to the rear. Release the bolt catch first, then the charging handle, so the bolt carrier group stays locked back.
steps.prose: The order of release is the whole technique: let go of the bolt catch while the handle is still held back, and the carrier settles onto the catch instead of running home. If it closes, do it again - the chamber check needs it open.
steps.quote: With your left thumb, press the bolt catch while simultaneously pulling the charging handle to the rear.
steps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Unloading the Firearm, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)

steps.title: Look into the chamber
steps.action: With the bolt locked back, look into the chamber and confirm it holds no fired or unfired cartridge and that the bore is not obstructed.
steps.prose: A look, not an assumption from the empty magazine well. FoldAR follows its unloading steps with its standing rule: treat the rifle as loaded anyway, and never point it at anyone.
steps.quote: Visually inspect and confirm that the chamber is clear of any fired/unfired cartridge or bore obstruction.
steps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Unloading the Firearm, printed p.21 (PDF p.21)
steps.warn: Regardless of accomplishing the above unloading procedure, always treat the firearm as if it were loaded and never point in the direction of anyone, no matter how near or far.

steps.title: Push the rear takedown pin from the left
steps.action: Find the front and rear takedown pins. With your finger or the tip of a bullet, press the left side of the rear takedown pin. If it is tight, squeeze the upper and lower receivers together while you press.
steps.prose: Squeezing the receivers takes the load off the pin, which is usually all a stiff pin needs. Do not reach for a hammer: the pin only has to start moving here.
steps.quote: With your finger or the tip of a bullet, press the left side of the rear takedown pin.
steps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Disassembly, printed p.29 (PDF p.29)

steps.title: Then the front pivot pin, the same way
steps.action: Press the left side of the front takedown pivot pin the same way.
steps.prose: Same direction, same technique: press from the left until the pin starts toward the right.
steps.quote: Repeat for the front takedown pivot pin.
steps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Disassembly, printed p.30 (PDF p.30)

steps.title: Pull both pins out from the right - rear first
steps.action: From the right side, pull the rear takedown pin the remaining way first, then the front takedown pin. Both pins are captive and stay in the lower receiver.
steps.prose: Rear first, then front - and the reverse when you put it back together. Captive means they stop on their own; pull until they stop, not until they come out.
steps.quote: Pull the rear takedown pin the remaining way from the right side first, then the front takedown pin (reverse for assembling).
steps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Disassembly, printed p.30 (PDF p.30)

steps.title: Bolt carrier group out of the upper
steps.action: Pull the charging handle rearward a few inches and remove the bolt carrier group.
steps.prose: A few inches is enough to bring the carrier to where you can grip it. Lift it out and set it on a clean surface; the charging handle follows it out of the upper.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle rearward a few inches and remove the bolt carrier group.
steps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Disassembly, printed p.31 (PDF p.31)

steps.title: Field strip complete - upper, lower, bolt carrier group
steps.action: That is the field strip: the upper and lower receivers apart, the bolt carrier group out. The deep clean below takes the bolt carrier group down and the barrel system off, which is as far as FoldAR's book goes.
steps.prose: The bore, the chamber end and the inside of the upper are all reachable from here. Everything past the bolt carrier group and the barrel system is, in FoldAR's words, for a certified gunsmith or FoldAR itself.
steps.quote: In the following section you will be shown how to properly field strip your FoldAR firearm to prepare it for cleaning and maintenance.
steps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Disassembly, printed p.29 (PDF p.29)

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retainer out of the side of the carrier
deepSteps.action: Remove the firing pin retainer from the side of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.prose: It is a small cotter-type pin and the first thing that holds the firing pin in. Put it straight into a tray - it is the part that goes missing.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin retainer located on the side of the carrier.
deepSteps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Disassembly, printed p.31 (PDF p.31)

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out of the rear of the carrier
deepSteps.action: With the retainer out, let the firing pin drop out of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: Tip the carrier tail-down and it falls free. If it does not, the retainer is not fully out.
deepSteps.quote: Now the firing pin will drop out of the carrier.
deepSteps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Disassembly, printed p.32 (PDF p.32)

deepSteps.title: Push the bolt back and turn the cam pin a quarter turn
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt rearward into the carrier, rotate the cam pin 90 degrees and lift it out.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt has to be pushed in first or the cam pin will not turn. A quarter turn lines the pin up to come out of its slot.
deepSteps.quote: Push the bolt rearward into the carrier and rotate the cam pin 90 degrees to remove.
deepSteps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Disassembly, printed p.32 (PDF p.32)

deepSteps.title: Bolt out of the carrier
deepSteps.action: Remove the bolt from the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: With the cam pin gone it slides out of the front of the carrier.
deepSteps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Disassembly, printed p.33 (PDF p.33)

deepSteps.title: Extractor pin out with the firing pin - mind the spring
deepSteps.action: Keep thumb pressure on the extractor while you use the firing pin to push the extractor pin out, then pull the pin free of the bolt. Lift the extractor out of the bolt.
deepSteps.prose: The extractor spring sits under the extractor and leaves with it if you are careless. Thumb pressure keeps the extractor from jumping as the pin clears.
deepSteps.quote: Lift out the extractor from the bolt, using caution not to lose the extractor spring.
deepSteps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Disassembly, printed p.33 (PDF p.33)

deepSteps.title: Optional: the barrel system off the upper, no tools
deepSteps.action: If you want the barrel system off for cleaning, disengage the barrel system takedown pin the same way as the lower receiver's takedown pins. Resting the muzzle on a supported surface with the barrel upright relaxes any binding on the pin.
deepSteps.prose: This is FoldAR's quick-detach system, and its book says cleaning is simpler with the barrel system off. When it goes back on, the locking hook and lever must be fully engaged before the rifle is fired.
deepSteps.quote: Disengage the barrel system takedown pin in the same manner as the front and rear takedown pins of the lower receiver.
deepSteps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Quick Detach Barrel System, printed p.14 (PDF p.14)

deepSteps.title: Leave the barrel set screws alone unless they are loose
deepSteps.action: Do not loosen the two set screws on the bottom of the forearm base. If they have come loose, retighten them only with the barrel system connected to the upper, unfolded and latched, using a 9/64-inch hex key at 28 in-lbs.
deepSteps.prose: They hold the barrel to the forearm base while the rifle is folded, and they are torqued with the barrel seated against the forearm base - which is why the rifle must be unfolded and latched when they go back in, so the barrel lines up with the upper.
deepSteps.quote: If these are loosened during maintenance, ensure that the barrel system is connected to the upper, unfolded, and latched before retightening these set screws using a 9/64” hex key with a torque setting of 28 in-lbs.
deepSteps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Quick Detach Barrel System, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)

deepSteps.title: Deep clean complete - FoldAR's stopping point
deepSteps.action: Stop here. The bolt carrier group parts are ready for cleaning, inspection and lubrication; anything further is for a certified gunsmith or FoldAR.
deepSteps.prose: FoldAR limits its book to what the average owner should take apart. Reassembly is these steps in reverse.
deepSteps.quote: These instructions are limited to disassembly techniques recommended to be limited to the average operator.
deepSteps.cite: FoldAR Operator’s Manual - Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — Rev 2.0 (Mar2026) — printed in every page's running header — Disassembly, printed p.34 (PDF p.34)

cleaning.name: PARTS & BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Scrub all accessible parts with light gun oil - a nylon brush on aluminium or steel, a brass brush on steel parts only
Wipe down with a lint-free cloth to show the baked-on carbon
Loosen the carbon with a carbon solvent cleaner, then scrub and wipe again

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: With a bore rod and a brass or copper brush and patch, scrub the bore back and forth with a copper and carbon removing solvent
Repeat until your patches show no carbon
If the rifle will be stowed for more than a week, run a patch soaked in gun oil
Never fire with excess oil in the bore - run a dry patch or bore snake before every shooting session
New barrel: clean the bore before and after the first session, and every 20 rounds for the first 200

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Once the parts are dry, spray them with a thin layer of gun oil

reassembly: If the barrel system was removed, refit it and re-engage the barrel system takedown pin; the locking hook and lever must be fully engaged before the rifle is fired.
Put the extractor spring and extractor back in the bolt and push the extractor pin home.
Slide the bolt into the carrier, refit the cam pin and turn it 90 degrees back.
Drop the firing pin into the rear of the carrier and refit the firing pin retainer from the side.
Put the charging handle and bolt carrier group back into the upper receiver.
Close the receivers and push the front takedown pin in, then the rear - the reverse of the order they came out.
fncheck: With the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty: the takedown pins should both be fully home; the locking hook should be on the clasp pin and the lever snapped flat against the barrel system - if the lever stands at a steep angle the hook is misplaced; the charging handle should run its full stroke and the bolt should lock back on the bolt catch and run home when the catch is pressed; and the selector should move between SAFE and FIRE.
